decision.reason: The qualified response preserves the successful control and shortens some unsuccessful cover attempts, but fresh wins fall from 8 to 6, completed sorties from 45 to 43, and ships lost rise from 9 to 11. Recorded asteroid and progress regressions remain.
limitations: Four new worlds are reused across seats and asteroid conditions; they are correlated samples.
One short-lived activation was omitted from sparse report snapshots. The original failed validation is preserved and two unchanged-binary diagnostic replays prove the activation and prefix parity.
Other per-capture event counts are retained-evidence lower bounds. A filtered direction or selected route is not a completed capture.
The asteroid replay reaches the sheltered landing, then fresh ground surveys fail after material revisions change. Its earlier later capture does not repair that original attempt.
Dispatch quotas exclude synchronous sensors, and desktop timings do not establish Raspberry Pi performance.
No successful physically executed capture through a newly probed omitted route was witnessed in this study; deterministic tests establish that selection path, not a gameplay benefit.
decision.next_investigation: Trace destination reconsideration after a blocked approach, including repeated returns to the same exposed destination. Determine whether failure context can guide a different achievable objective before another policy change.
